rows.description: A child who hurt a friend apologises and helps fix things, then is able to play again. Forgiveness of oneself follows real repair more easily than pure guilt or excuses.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager replays an embarrassing moment or a harsh remark for days. Harsh self-review feels like accountability but mostly produces shame and avoidance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A friend hears someone say it was not my fault every time. Self-forgiveness requires owning the harm first, whereas excuses skip that step and leave the guilt unresolved.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult who wasted a year or hurt a partner keeps punishing themselves through lost opportunities. Learning that the past self did the best it knew at the time allows moving forward.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person speaks to themselves after failure as they would to a friend, naming the error and the effort. Self-compassion supports better change than self-contempt does.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child plans tomorrow's picnic and is sure it will be sunny. Early hope is simple trust that adults will provide a good future, and broken promises damage it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child who practised spelling hopes to do well on the test and works harder because of it. Hope with a path attached keeps effort alive, while wishing alone does not.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who failed an exam concludes that everything is ruined and nothing will change. Hopelessness narrows thinking, and one adult or friend offering a concrete next step can widen it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A friend responds to another's despair by staying, listening, and pointing to a small next step, not by insisting everything will be fine. Hope is passed through presence more than promises.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult applies for jobs or postings knowing many will fail, yet continues. Mature hope accepts uncertainty and still acts, unlike wishful hope that waits for fate.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
